units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 47b:10">Snh. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>ק׳ חדש</he> a fresh grave (that has been dug but not used).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 47b:7">Ib.</cite> <he>ק׳ בנין</he> a grave on which something has been built, i.e. an arched grave (not flat).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 47b:11">Ib.</cite> <he>שלשה קברות הן ק׳ הנמצא</he> there are three kinds of graves (with reference to law): a grave that has been discovered (a fresh grave in which somebody was buried without the consent of the owner of the ground); <he>ק׳ הידוע</he> a known grave (in which one was buried with the owner’s consent); <he>ק׳ המזיק את הרבים</he> a grave which interferes with public comfort (made in a thoroughfare).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 9:2:6">Y. Naz. IX, 57ᵈ</cite> top., v. <cite ref="V00119"><he>תְּהוֹם</he></cite>. Ohol. XVII, 1 <he>החורש את הק׳</he> if one passes the plough over a grave.
Koh. R. to VII, 8 וכיון שקברוהו … את קִבְרוֹ when they had buried him (Elisha-Aḥer), a fire came to burn his grave; a. v. fr.—Pl. קְבָרִים, קְבָרוֹת.

<cite ref="Taanit 25b:4">Taan. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>תקנתם ק׳ וכ׳</he> have you prepared graves for yourselves (are you ready to die)? <cite ref="Taanit 22b:16">Ib. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>שלא יהא בתיהם קִבְרֵיהֶם</he> that their houses may not become their graves (that their dwellings may not fall down from excessive rains); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 5:2:5">Y. Yoma V, 42ᶜ</cite> top <he>שלא יעשו … קִבְרֵיהֶן</he>.
<cite ref="Chagigah 22b:6">Ḥag. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>נשתטח על קִבְרֵי וכ׳</he> he prostrated himself over the graves of &c.
<cite ref="Yevamot 47b:9">Yeb. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>שני ק׳ נמסרו וכ׳</he> the court has charge of two burial places (for culprits).
Snh. VI, 5 ולא היו קוברין אותו בקִבְרוֹת אבותיו they did not bury him (the culprit) in the burial place of their ancestors; a. fr.—בֵּית הקברות (abbr. בה״ק) cemetery; pl. בָּתֵּי ק׳.

Ber. 18ᵇ הלך ולן בב״הק he went and spent the night in the cemetery. Snh. l. c. (46ᵇ) שני בתי ק׳ וכ׳ two burial grounds were at the disposal of the courts, one for those put to death by the sword, and one &c.; a. fr.—Trnsf. uterus (containing an embryo).
<cite ref="Niddah 21a:44">Nidd. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>באיפשר לפתיחת הק׳ וכ׳</he> they differ as to whether the uterus can open (to pass the embryo) without discharging blood.

<cite ref="Shabbat 129a:2">Sabb. 129ᵃ</cite> <he>חיה כל זמן שהק׳ פתוח וכ׳</he> for a woman in confinement you must violate the Sabbath laws as long as the uterus is open, whether she says that she needs it or that she needs it not.

<cite ref="Shabbat 129a:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מאימתי פתיחת הק׳</he> when does the opening of the womb begin (in regard to Sabbath laws)?; <he>עד מתי … הק׳</he> how long is it considered open? Ohol. VII, 4 <he>אין לנפלים פ׳ הק׳ וכ׳</he> in the case of abortions the laws of levitical cleanness connected with the opening of the womb do not apply, unless &c., v. <cite ref="Q00797"><he>פִּיקָא</he> I</cite>; Tosef. ib. VIII, 8; a. fr.
